headline: Nationals sign Jacob Young to extension, locking down another core player
author: Danielle Allentuck

paragraphs.text: The Washington Nationals have agreed to a contract extension with outfielder Jacob Young, according to a person familiar with the situation. The deal would lock in the center fielder for at least the next four years.
The person spoke on the condition of anonymity Friday because they weren’t authorized to publicly discuss the contract.
Young’s new deal — which is worth $23 million, according to reports — would buy out his three arbitration-eligible seasons and one year of free agency. There’s also an option for an additional year.

It’s the second extension handed out by Paul Toboni, the Nationals’ president of baseball operations, since he took over a year ago as the team invests in its core. Starting pitcher Cade Cavalli signed a four-year, $47 million extension in September.

Young, 27, debuted in 2023 and became a staple in Washington’s outfield a year later. He’s always been known for his strong defensive skills — his fielding range ranks in the 96th percentile — and he was named a Gold Glove finalist in 2024 and 2025.

Last offseason, Young put an increased emphasis on his hitting. He spent part of his offseason at Driveline, an advanced data-driven hitting lab in Kent, Washington. There, he worked on his swing with a trio of weighted bats. His average bat speed increased to 69.6 mph this season, up from 68.3 mph a year ago.
Those changes helped him hit a career-high 10 home runs in 140 games, compared to five in his previous 303. He also hit .252 with a .708 OPS last season, both the best marks of his career.

The Nationals’ outfield already seemed set for the long haul, with Dylan Crews, James Wood and Daylen Lile not becoming free agents until at least 2031. Now, they have at least one extra year of Young, who would have become a free agent in 2030.
